_note: HARD loom-core eval set (18 Q) — multi-file / behavioral / long-construct / semantic-distance questions that do NOT saturate retrieval, unlike questions.loomcore.json (which the bge stack aces 16/16). Built to give Slice 3 (chunking bake-off) discriminating signal. Authored + adversarially verified 2026-06-25.

questions.question: In the HUD's dispatch-a-task-to-an-agent flow, when the chosen target agent currently has no active session, what does the system still do, and where does it get the originating session for the work handoff it creates?
questions.answer: It skips task creation (empty session_id) but still creates the handoff; the source session is resolved by resolveDispatchSourceSessionID: explicit source_session_id, else cached hud_dispatch_session, else the active session of the hud-dispatcher agent, else a new dispatcher session in namespace loom-core/hud-dispatch.

questions.question: When the bridge builds an agent's handoff inbox, how does it keep dispatched-task routing deterministic if the server returns an empty summary for a handoff?
questions.answer: If the instructions text begins with the '[Dispatched] ' prefix, the inbox builder elevates the first line of the instructions to be the summary, overriding the empty server-provided summary.

questions.question: After the bridge unwraps an MCP tool-result envelope, the inner text payload won't always parse as plain JSON. What does the bridge do when a direct JSON decode of that text fails, before giving up?
questions.answer: It falls back to decoding the text as TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) via mcp.DecodeTOONToJSON, then unmarshals the resulting JSON; only if that also fails does it return a decode error.

questions.question: When agent_session_start is called and an active session already exists for that agent in the same namespace, what determines whether the service returns the existing session unchanged versus closing it and opening a brand-new one, and how does the response signal that the old session was reclaimed?
questions.answer: It checks whether the agent's presence heartbeat is stale (isAgentHeartbeatStale). Live heartbeat returns the existing session with already_existed=true; stale heartbeat treats it as an orphaned crash, ends it, creates a new session, and sets recovered_from to the old session ID.

questions.question: Qdrant returns HTTP 404 for both a missing collection and a missing point. In this Qdrant client, how does it decide a 404 means the collection is gone, and which read operation actually surfaces that distinction to its caller instead of silently returning an empty result?
questions.answer: doJSON maps a 404 to ErrCollectionNotFound only when the path targets the client's collection AND the response body contains the substring 'collection'. GetPoint propagates ErrCollectionNotFound; Search/Scroll/GetPoints/Count swallow it and return empty.

questions.question: In the hard-enforced multi-file claim path used so a parallel slice never half-claims its file set, what happens when one of the requested files is already held by another active agent, and how are already-expired holds and the requester's own existing holds treated?
questions.answer: AcquireEnforced is all-or-nothing via two passes: pass one detects conflicts without mutating and returns the conflicting files acquiring nothing; holds by the same requester are skipped (idempotent) and expired holds (ExpiresAt past) are ignored; only with zero conflicts does pass two acquire all.

questions.question: When the cache is configured for the Redis backend but the Redis server cannot be reached at startup, what does the store factory hand back to the caller, and does the caller get an error?
questions.answer: New() returns no error; when NewRedisStore fails it logs a warning ('redis cache unavailable, falling back to memory') and returns NewMemoryStore(), so the caller silently gets a working in-memory store.

questions.question: In this cache layer, ordinary Redis read/write operations time out far sooner than the prefix-wide bulk clear. What are the two timeout durations, and which operation gets the longer one?
questions.answer: Per-operation Get/Set/Invalidate use redisOpTimeout = 500ms; InvalidateAll (the SCAN-based bulk clear) uses a 5-second timeout.

questions.question: For a standalone (non-cluster) Redis connection, if a password is embedded in the connection URL but no separate password is provided in the config struct, which password is actually used to authenticate?
questions.answer: The URL's password is kept: ParseURL sets opts.Password from the URL, and cfg.Password only overrides it when cfg.Password is non-empty. An empty config password leaves the URL password intact.

questions.question: In the codebase indexer's embedding layer, search queries and document writes are deliberately treated differently when the primary embedding provider is down: one path is allowed to use a backup model and the other is not. Which operation refuses the backup and why, and what is the caller expected to do instead?
questions.answer: EmbedQuery refuses the secondary embedder (primary only); EmbedDocuments does fall back. Reason: a same-dimension secondary model lives in a different vector space, so a secondary-space query against a primary-space corpus is noise. The caller should degrade to keyword search.

questions.question: During an incremental (non-full-refresh) index run, how does the pipeline avoid both re-parsing an unchanged file AND re-embedding chunks whose text it has seen before, and what two attributes must match for a previously stored vector to be reused for a chunk?
questions.answer: Per file it fetches a Qdrant preflight (GetFilePreflight): if the stored module ContentHash equals the current file content hash, the file is skipped before parsing; otherwise the preflight's EmbeddingCache is reused per chunk. A vector is reused only if the chunk content_hash AND the embed_model both match.

questions.question: Why do the per-batch writes during an index job not wait for the data to be committed, and what happens to the job's reported status if the single round-trip at the end of the run fails?
questions.answer: Bulk upsert batches run with wait=false so Qdrant queues WAL+HNSW work in the background (avoiding EOF on loaded nodes); durability is proved by a single trailing Flush. That flush is non-fatal: on error it records a soft flush warning (recordFlushWarning) and the job still reports status=done because prior writes are durable via WAL fsync.

questions.question: In the daemon call pipeline, a slow local stdio MCP server can hit a receive-side deadline while the subprocess is still alive and serving other concurrent callers. Tearing it down on that first timeout would drop every other in-flight caller. How does the daemon avoid that, and what finally forces a full transport teardown and respawn?
questions.answer: On a local recv timeout, transportFailure keeps the subprocess alive and returns an internal error, incrementing a per-server consecutive recv-timeout streak; only once the streak reaches the breaker threshold (default 3, LOOM_LOCAL_RECV_TIMEOUT_BREAKER) does it tear down (ClearServer+stopServerProc+respawn). A successful recv resets the streak.

questions.question: When the daemon forwards a tool call to an upstream server and reads back a JSON-RPC response, what does it do if the response's id does not equal the request id it sent, and why is that check there?
questions.answer: It treats the id mismatch as transport corruption (a stale/interleaved response on a shared stdio transport), logs 'response ID mismatch ... (possible transport corruption)', and routes it through the retry/transportFailure path so the connection is recycled and the caller gets a clear error instead of wrong data.

questions.question: A loopback client issues a tool call like 'agent_context__<tool>' and agent_context is on the cluster-delegation list, yet the daemon still launches a local subprocess for it instead of relaying it through the in-cluster hub. Which configuration condition causes the daemon to skip cluster delegation for that server?
questions.answer: The server being listed in WarmOnStart: hubDelegateEligible returns false for any server in WarmOnStart because warmed servers are meant to run as local subprocesses, so delegation is skipped and the call routes to the local pool.

questions.question: In the loom MCP proxy, when a client invokes a downstream tool, how does the proxy decide how long to wait before timing out that single tool call, and how does a per-server timeout configured in routing.timeouts interact with a timeout the caller embedded in the tool arguments?
questions.answer: It derives a per-call timeout from the arguments JSON (timeout_seconds/timeoutSeconds/timeout) via proxyDeriveTimeoutFromArguments; a per-server override from proxyRoutingTimeouts is applied only if its duration is greater than the argument-derived one (it can lengthen but never shorten it).

questions.question: When a connecting agent identifies itself as claude-code, codex, or claude and no explicit tool profile is set, which proxy tool-shaping profile gets selected and what is the resulting maximum number of tools advertised to that client?
questions.answer: resolveProxyToolFilter maps those hints to the llm-core profile (proxyToolProfileLLMCore), which with no explicit max applies a cap of 140 tools (proxyToolLimitLLM); selectCoreDeveloperTools builds the curated subset under that limit.

questions.question: When a proxied tool returns more data than the configured response cap, the proxy trims text content, but it handles screenshot/picture payloads completely differently. What does it do with an oversized image payload and why?
questions.answer: Image payloads are atomic: kept whole if they fit the remaining image byte budget, otherwise dropped entirely (replaced with a short text note) rather than truncated, to avoid emitting a partial base64 data URL that would break clients like Codex/OpenAI.
